coral-edwardsen.text: Called technology "the hot issue right now"; said it has a place in classrooms but students should first build strong foundations in reading, writing and critical thinking rather than relying on devices.

source.title: The Acorn: Two challengers eye school board (2026-08-27)

coral-edwardsen.text: Said one focus would be "How do we effectively communicate with our communities in order to make LVUSD the absolute best it can be?" and stressed a deliberative process including input from teachers and families.

source.title: The Acorn: Two challengers eye school board (2026-08-27)

coral-edwardsen.text: Campaign priorities: curriculum with clear standards-aligned goals; students as "good stewards of technology"; school safety including mental health; budgeting by working with teachers and staff.

source.title: Coral Edwardsen for LVUSD: Issues (campaign site)

coral-edwardsen.text: Endorsed by the Las Virgenes Educators Association (teachers union) and all five sitting LVUSD board members.

source.title: Coral Edwardsen for LVUSD: Endorsements (campaign site)

dallas-lawrence.text: At a Sept. 15, 2026 board meeting called for a stronger screen policy, including middle and high school screen limits and a complete device ban in TK and kindergarten: "We have allowed things to seep into our classrooms that are not proven."

source.title: The Acorn: Lengthy school board meeting addresses student screen policy (2026-09-24)

dallas-lawrence.text: Voted for the districtwide campus cellphone ban adopted in early 2025, which passed narrowly.

source.title: The Acorn: Books, cellphones and social media — a whirlwind school year (2025-12-25)

dallas-lawrence.text: On a teacher placed on leave over Charlie Kirk posts: "This was not about politics. It was about ... keeping our children safe. There is no place for violent discourse from school employees. Period."

source.title: The Acorn: Las Virgenes teacher placed on leave over Charlie Kirk comments (2025-09-15)

dallas-lawrence.text: (2024) Opposed giving the sheriff's department "24/7, unfettered, unreviewed, unsupervised access" to campus camera feeds, and sought a 90-day review.

source.title: The Acorn: School district gives sheriff OK to monitor campus cameras full time (2024-12-05)

dallas-lawrence.text: Asked in a May 2026 screen-time discussion, "When is technology too soon?", noting data suggesting 30 minutes a day for i-Ready.

source.title: The Acorn: Parents want more limits placed on screen time (2026-05-21)

angela-cutbill.text: Backing tighter screen limits: "I don't think it's pulling the rug out from under our teachers to do this, but my God, I want to pull the headphones off the 5-year-old."

source.title: The Acorn: Lengthy school board meeting addresses student screen policy (2026-09-24)

angela-cutbill.text: Voted for the districtwide campus cellphone ban adopted in early 2025.

source.title: The Acorn: Books, cellphones and social media — a whirlwind school year (2025-12-25)

angela-cutbill.text: (2024) As board president, supported letting the sheriff's department monitor campus cameras full time: "They've kind of assured us, they're not looking to just sit and study kids."

source.title: The Acorn: School district gives sheriff OK to monitor campus cameras full time (2024-12-05)

sandra-pope.text: In an Aug. 2026 letter: "We cannot afford to 'pause' the inclusion of technology in our classrooms," criticizing the parent group Schools Beyond Screens and defending the district technology committee.

source.title: The Acorn letter by Sandra Pope: Too late to pause technology in class (2026-08-27)

sandra-pope.text: Later apologized at a board meeting for that letter, saying it was dismissive of parents' concerns, and asked the board to consider a two-year screen-time policy with committees studying the issue first.

source.title: The Acorn: Lengthy school board meeting addresses student screen policy (2026-09-24)

sandra-pope.text: Proposed bringing together school districts, law enforcement and tech experts to develop a K-12 curriculum "that keeps kids safe from the second they turn on a computer."

source.title: The Acorn: Two challengers eye school board (2026-08-27)

sandra-pope.text: Praised district leadership as "very progressive" and said some parents feel the board lacks "a good vehicle for communication" and transparency.

source.title: The Acorn: Two challengers eye school board (2026-08-27)
